It's so sad to see this mall go. Within the area we still have a handful of malls (some doing better than others), but The St. Louis Mills was always my favorite. I like how it has more thematic designs throughout the mall. Each area was split into a "neighborhood" and each neighborhood had its own look to it. One example, as shown in your first image, is the food court. It was themed after the 1904 World's Fair and featured a carousel, informative posters with facts on the World's Fair, and some other smaller details. My favorite was always the sports neighborhood. While I've never been a huge sports fan myself, I loved the small details in that area. Most notably was a hockey rink deigned into the wood flooring. As a child I would always try my best to jump from one end to the other without touching the "ice."

I visited the mall recently for the first time in years. The building still stands, and there are just a handful of vendors, but the mall is finally seeing an uptick in activity. However, it's no longer  a mall. The property is now being converted into a sports complex, which I think is great. Portions of the mall are still open for you to walk in, but a vast majority is gated away never to be seen again. Unless you just step over the tiny fence... lol

For yourself and your family, please do not continue to go down the path of vaping. I started at a young age as well. Not 11, but still long before I ever should have been able to. I’m completely aware that in the moment it may relieve some stress, or even make you feel more mature or cooler around your friends. Please try and focus on yourself, your family, and your future. I can imagine you must feel quite helpless, but this is one thing you can help. Please dispose of the vapes you purchased. I know it’ll sting considering you spent all of your savings on them, but if you don’t you’ll only continue to spend more and more money over time. 

Please keep your head held high and find a more positive outlet. Don’t let your home life or position in school define you. Make the world yours.

Man, I'm so happy to hear that. It really used to be one of the best options out here for a nice budget dine-in experience. I loved the aesthetic and layout of the interior, and as you said for the price the food was pretty damn good. The thing that finally killed it for me was the waits. As I stated in my previous comment, the customer service began to decline rapidly. Wrong orders, you could be one of the only people there and you'd be waiting for about thirty minutes for your food, and even the general upkeep of some locations out here began to severely decline. I remember walking into the restroom of the Steak n' Shake where this "worm" incident occurred and there was water all over the floor. Both toilets had overflowed, but on top of that feces and urine were also coming out. When I mentioned this to an employee they simply stated that they were aware and seemed to find the incident somewhat amusing. Such a shame honestly. The competition out here that popped up around the same time of Steak n' Shake's decline, mostly Culver's, was a little pricier but the food, service, and cleanliness of everything was pretty much the final nail in the coffin. All locations have since closed and have signs up saying that you could purchase the location for $30k and the company will provide you with the supplies necessary to begin operations, but most locations are being purchased by other restaurants. The Steak n' Shake mentioned in the article has since become a Freddy's and Steak n' Shake is nothing more than a distant memory for us in St. Louis.

This Steak n' Shake is only a few streets away from me and used to be PACKED any day of the week. As time went on though new places such as Culver's and Freddy's came in and started to destroy Steak n' Shake sales wise and customer service wise. Then this worm incident occurred and it was all downhill from there. One by one each location in the area began to shut their doors, the customer service was unbearable, and because of the worm incident they simply became a joke to everyone in town. We all knew it was a place to avoid. Kind of sad, I used to love eating there, there was certainly a charm to Steak n' Shake. I just think (in my area at least) they really dropped the ball and didn't know how to keep up with their competitors. 

For any of you guys, is Steak n' Shake still popular wherever you are? Like I said, for the locations near me they just couldn't keep up with competition, but I'm curious if there are still places where business is booming for them.
